cases.question: Was the same AI tested more than once under the same setup to check whether its score stays consistent?
cases.description: The researchers state that they evaluated the fixed model once only and performed no repeat runs under that setup.

cases.question: Was the same AI tested more than once under the same setup to check whether its score stays consistent?
cases.description: The report gives one aggregate score for each of three models. It does not state how many runs produced each score.

cases.question: Were the test problems and the answers used to mark them checked for errors during development?
cases.description: During development, two reviewers checked every test problem and its reference answer for errors. They identified and corrected mistakes in both.

cases.question: Were the test problems and the answers used to mark them checked for errors during development?
cases.description: During development, reviewers checked the wording of every test problem. The developers explicitly state that reference answers were not checked.

cases.question: Was it tested how much scores change when instructions, presentation or the testing setup change?
cases.description: The researchers compared scores for the same model after rewording the instructions and changing the screen layout. They reported how scores changed.

cases.question: Was it tested how much scores change when instructions, presentation or the testing setup change?
cases.description: The researchers ran the same model five times using identical instructions and settings. They explicitly state that no changed setup was tested.

cases.question: Was the marking method checked for mistakes, such as software bugs, mistakes when reading the AI's answer, or inconsistent human or AI judges?
cases.description: Responses are marked by exact string matching. The marking rules are documented, but the supplied report says nothing about checking the program.

cases.question: Are the test materials and methods available in enough detail for someone else to repeat the evaluation or examine how it was done?
cases.description: A sample of tasks and scoring instructions is available for inspection. The remaining tasks and the settings needed to repeat the reported evaluation are explicitly unavailable, and no other inspection access exists.

cases.question: Is there evidence for any claim that the scores show how well an AI system will perform beyond the problems in this test?
cases.description: The authors claim only the observed scores on the exact tasks administered. The stated use is to describe those runs; no prediction about new tasks or wider performance is proposed.

cases.question: Is there evidence for any claim that the scores show how well an AI system will perform beyond the problems in this test?
cases.description: The authors claim that scores predict performance on unseen tasks sampled from the same specified task population. A separate, prespecified study tests that exact prediction on new tasks and reports a positive relationship with uncertainty estimates and no contradictory findings in the supplied record.
